n: Another message. Chapter 18 is one of the clearest teachings in scripture on personal responsibility and repentance.

f.w: The word of the LORD came unto me again

n: People were quoting a proverb: “The parents ate sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are on edge.” In other words, “We’re being punished for our ancestors’ sins—it isn’t our fault.”

f.w: The fathers have eaten sour grapes
set on edge
f.g: Made dull or sensitive, as when eating something sour.

n: God swears this excuse will no longer be used in Israel.

f.w: As I live

n: Every soul belongs to God—parent and child alike—and each person answers for his own sins. The Second Article of Faith expresses a similar principle.

f.w: all souls are mine
the soul that sinneth, it shall die

n: Ezekiel gives a case study across three generations. First, a righteous man who does what is just and right…

f.w: just

n: …who doesn’t feast at mountain idol shrines, worship idols, commit adultery, or break the purity laws of marriage…

f.w: eaten upon the mountains
f.g: Taken part in sacrificial meals at hilltop idol shrines.

f.w: a menstruous woman

n: …who doesn’t exploit others, returns a poor borrower’s pledge, never robs, feeds the hungry, and clothes the naked…

f.w: restored to the debtor his pledge
f.g: Returned the cloak or tool taken as collateral, so the poor were not left without necessities.

f.w: hath given his bread to the hungry

n: …who doesn’t charge interest to the needy, avoids wrongdoing, and judges fairly between people…

f.w: usury
f.g: Interest on loans; Israelites were forbidden to charge it to fellow Israelites in need.

f.w: increase
f.g: Profit or interest taken on a loan.

n: …and who follows God’s laws faithfully. Such a person is righteous and will surely live.

f.w: he shall surely live

n: Second generation: suppose that righteous man has a son who becomes violent and bloodthirsty…

f.w: a robber, a shedder of blood

n: …who does none of his father’s good deeds but joins idol feasts and commits adultery…

f.w: defiled his neighbour's wife

n: …who oppresses the poor, robs, keeps pledges, and worships idols…

f.w: oppressed the poor and needy

n: …and lends at interest. Will he live because his father was righteous? No. His blood is on his own head.

f.w: his blood shall be upon him
f.g: He alone is responsible for his death.

n: Third generation: suppose this wicked man has a son who sees his father’s sins, thinks it over, and chooses differently…

f.w: considereth
f.g: Reflects carefully—the first step toward a different life.

n: …who avoids idols and adultery…

f.w: lifted up his eyes to the idols
f.g: Looked to idols for help or worship.

n: …who oppresses no one, returns pledges, never robs, and feeds and clothes the needy…

f.w: hath covered the naked with a garment

n: …and keeps God’s laws. He will not die for his father’s sins; he will surely live. No one is trapped by their family’s past.

f.w: he shall not die for the iniquity of his father

n: His father, however, will die for his own oppression and violence.

f.w: spoiled his brother by violence

n: The people object: “Why shouldn’t the son bear his father’s guilt?” God’s answer is firm: if the son does right, he will live.

f.w: doth not the son bear the iniquity of the father?

n: The principle stated plainly: each person bears his own righteousness or wickedness. Consequences can pass between generations, but guilt does not.

f.w: The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father

n: Even better news: if a wicked person turns from all his sins and does what is right, he will surely live.

f.w: if the wicked will turn from all his sins

n: His past sins will not be held against him; he will live because of the righteousness he now chooses. God truly forgives.

f.w: they shall not be mentioned unto him

n: One of the most tender verses in the Old Testament: God takes no pleasure in anyone’s death; he wants the wicked to turn and live.

f.w: Have I any pleasure at all that the wicked should die?

n: The reverse is also true: if a righteous person turns to wickedness and stays there, his former goodness won’t save him. Enduring to the end matters.

f.w: when the righteous turneth away from his righteousness

n: People complain, “The Lord’s way isn’t fair!” God answers: “Is it my way that is unfair—or yours?”

f.w: The way of the Lord is not equal

n: A righteous person who turns to sin and dies in it dies for the sin he committed.

f.w: dieth in them

n: A wicked person who turns from wickedness and does right saves his life.

f.w: he shall save his soul alive

n: Because he thoughtfully turns from all his transgressions, he will live. Repentance begins with reflection.

f.w: he considereth, and turneth away

n: Still Israel says God is unfair. God repeats his challenge: it is your ways that are crooked.

f.w: are not your ways unequal?
f.g: Isn’t it your ways that are unjust?

n: God will judge each person by his own ways. So repent and turn, so that sin won’t be your downfall.

f.w: every one according to his ways
Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions

n: Throw away your sins and “make you a new heart and a new spirit.” In 11:19 and 36:26 God gives the new heart; here Israel must also act. Repentance is both God’s gift and our choice. “Why will you die?”

f.w: make you a new heart and a new spirit
why will ye die

n: The chapter ends with God’s heart laid bare: he takes no pleasure in anyone’s death. “Turn yourselves, and live.”

f.w: turn yourselves, and live ye
